en: This agent has 2 tools, summarize text and
create PDF, because the agent I'm building
here is there to help the user either
summarize text and/or also create PDF files
based on that summary or based on something
totally else.
And if we go back to the workflow overview,
we can see those tools here. These tools are
just end-to-end workflows, but very simple
workflows.
Summarize text, for example, receives the
text input. That is the trigger node here.
This is a workflow that is meant to be used
from other workflows and those other
workflows have to pass some data into this
workflow here, the text specifically. And
then I have one other node here, a summarize
node,
which is just a prebuilt node built into
n8n,
which in the end works like the example you
saw earlier in the course in the AI workflow
section, which allows us to construct a
custom prompt using this dynamic n8n syntax
here, which combines some hardcoded text
from us with some dynamically extracted
text.
Or dynamically provided text. In this case,
that is just the input text received by that
workflow, by that tool workflow.
And then we sent this to
a model, to an AI model, along with some
system prompt here regarding how that
summary should be created.
And that is just a little summarizer node
provided by N8n.
I'm using GPT-5.6 Sol, but we could use a
simpler model there too.
The pricing, of course, will depend on which
model you use.
And then the output seems to go into the
void, but technically that will not happen
since this is a workflow that will be used
by another workflow. The result of that
workflow will simply flow back into the
agent here in the end. And this agent node
will orchestrate and will send tool results
back to the model, will handle the model
requests. If the model wants to use a tool,
it will invoke the tool. So that is what
this built-in AI agent node in n8n does. It
orchestrates the agent and acts as the
harness for the agent, so to say.
Most importantly, the agent loop is inside
of that node, so to say. So we don't need to
write our own code for that. That's the idea
behind a visual workflow builder like n8n.
Instead, this agent node takes care of all
of that.
Well, and the create PDF workflow is just
another tool which
uses some code, actually some hard-coded
code, not code generated by the model
dynamically, but some code written in
advance by me that will just build a PDF and
then store that on your disk. And we'll see
where that file ends up later.
These are the 2 tools, and then they are
combined and attached to the agent here in
the main agent workflow. And now we can give
this a try.
